title: The month onion prices jumped across India
summary: In August 2008, the median onion market moved +36.9% in a month, 3.8 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 3.8σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for onion, across 346 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: August 2008
scenes.caption: Onion prices across 346 markets that reported in both July 2008 and August 2008.

scenes.headline: Median move +36.9%
scenes.caption: The typical market's onion price jumped 36.9% in one month. 92% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 3.8× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 3.8 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Madhya Pradesh
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 30 reporting markets in Madhya Pradesh had a median change of +100.0%.

scenes.headline: Indri
scenes.caption: Indri (Haryana), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹400 → ₹750 per quintal (+87.5%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.
